item.title: San Francisco's car crime has plunged. How much credit does Flock deserve?
item.description: San Francisco leaders say AI-powered cameras helped drive a dramatic decline in car crime. We examine the evidence — and whether the city can keep its high-tech dragnet without sacrificing civil liberties.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Failed 'torturous' execution attempt on Christa Pike reignites death penalty debate
item.description: The botched execution in Tennessee of Christa Pike, who survived despite being subject to two doses of lethal injection on Wednesday, has reignited furious debate about the death penalty in the U.S.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: The U.S. Senate is up for grabs. Can this Ohio Democrat win back working class votes?
item.description: After 32 years in Congress, Ohio's Sherrod Brown lost his Senate seat in 2024 as many working class voters turned out for Trump. Now Brown is counting on union voters to send him back to Washington.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: A judge permanently dismisses former Olympian's Reflecting Pool charges
item.description: Citing "exceptional circumstances," a D.C. judge has ruled that the federal government cannot refile its Reflecting Pool charges against David Hearn, despite pressure from President Trump to do so.

item.title: AI data centers: How much are ratepayers on the hook for?
item.description: Data centers consume large amounts of power and require upgrading infrastructure. But it's difficult to determine how much residential customers benefit and how much they actually pay for the benefit.

item.title: COMIC: How the census gives your state power (and what Trump wants to change)
item.description: The census is used to determine how much say your state has in Congress and the Electoral College. President Trump failed to alter it during his first term, but he's trying again ahead of 2030.
